title: D2 Data Audit
description: Row and value flow from bronze to gold, per entity, written to the warehouse so Power BI can report on it. Answers 'where did the rows go' with a number rather than an opinion. AUTHORITATIVE: validation fails the build.

target.description: Where the audit lands. The warehouse, not a lakehouse: the semantic model reads DirectLake from there, so an audit written anywhere else could not be reported on alongside the numbers it audits.

view.description: Reporting view over the table, e.g. bi.vw_layer_audit.

write_mode.description: append keeps history, so a shrinking row count is visible as a trend rather than only as today's number. overwrite keeps the latest run only.

retain_runs.description: Runs kept when appending. Absent means keep everything.

entities.description: One per business entity, naming what it is called at each layer so counts are comparable. The whole point is that bronze_commerce_order_items, stg_order_items and dbo.fct_sales are the same thing measured three times.

grain_changes.description: Set where a layer legitimately changes the row count for a reason other than loss -- an SCD2 dimension holds one row per VERSION, so its count exceeds silver's without anything being wrong. Suppresses the shrinkage warning for that entity.

layers.description: At least two layers, or there is nothing to compare.

table.description: Unqualified for a lakehouse table; schema-qualified for a warehouse one.

measure.description: Money or quantity column summed alongside the row count. A count alone hides value moving without rows moving -- a corrected subtotal changes the total while every row survives.

filter.description: Spark SQL predicate applied before counting, e.g. is_current = true for the current slice of an SCD2 dimension.

quarantine.description: Table holding rows this layer rejected. Counted separately so kept + rejected can be reconciled against the layer above, which is what turns an unexplained drop into an explained one.
